open_errors.issue: In ch 4 Devan tells Neela he has 'watched him write grey-wax letters for six years' and concludes they are the queen's. That means he already knows the queen has been receiving letters for six years. In ch 8, Rema's thanks for 'six years of faithful letters' is presented as the reveal: 'He had guessed the palace. He had not guessed six years of it.' F501 also has him realise the six-year span only at that supper.
open_errors.fix: Remove the six-year span from Devan's ch 4 argument so the ch 8 reveal still lands.

patches.find: I've watched him write grey-wax letters for six years. They go with the palace rider.
patches.replace: I've watched him write grey-wax letters every month. They go with the palace rider.

open_errors.issue: The book counts the time since Ammu's death and Neela's binding too short. The binding was at the second dusk at the Resin House, followed by the return, Ittan's arrival two days later, the sealing, the vow and nine days of rain. That makes ch 1 about sixteen days after Ammu died, yet the text says 'Not two weeks dead'. In ch 7 (about five days later) Pachan correctly says 'three weeks ago'. In ch 14, about four weeks after the binding, the empty cage is called 'three weeks cold'.
open_errors.fix: Bring both counts in line with Pachan's 'three weeks' in ch 7.

patches.find: Ammu. Not two weeks dead, and her thumb of resin sat in the cord pouch against Neela's hip.
patches.replace: Ammu. Not three weeks dead, and her thumb of resin sat in the cord pouch against Neela's hip.

patches.find: This one held the shape of her, three weeks cold, kept for the day she was brought back.
patches.replace: This one held the shape of her, a month cold, kept for the day she was brought back.

open_errors.issue: Ch 1 says Neela 'had been a name for nine days', which implies she only became 'Neela' recently. Elsewhere she has carried the name for years: Ammu called it across a courtyard (ch 32), and 'Neela is what I did with the years after' (ch 20). What is new since the vow is being a name in the open.
open_errors.fix: Make the line about being named publicly, not about having a name at all.

patches.find: She had been twenty-one years a number. She had been a name for nine days.
patches.replace: She had been twenty-one years a number. She had been a name in front of a whole household only since the vow.

open_errors.issue: In ch 2 Devan 'had never asked why' Neela keeps wide of the west stair. But ch 10, ch 16 and ch 22 (and F328, F518) all say he once asked her why she takes the turn on the eleventh step, and she answered 'I don't know'.

patches.find: He had never asked why, and he did not ask now.
patches.replace: He had asked her once, about the eleventh step, and she had said she didn't know. He did not ask now.

open_errors.issue: First Guard's 'left hand went to her left cuff and closed on it', but a hand cannot grip its own cuff. In ch 3 it is her right hand that closes on her left cuff over the wrist seam.
open_errors.fix: Change it to her right hand.

patches.find: Then her left hand went to her left cuff and closed on it, and stayed there.
patches.replace: Then her right hand went to her left cuff and closed on it, and stayed there.

open_errors.issue: In ch 3 Eravi applies the salve 'with the tip of his little finger'. In ch 5 Neela recalls it as 'the salve on Eravi's thumb'.

patches.find: The salve on Eravi's thumb had been the first.
patches.replace: The salve on Eravi's finger had been the first.

open_errors.issue: Neela remembers Devan saying 'Find me in daylight' on the rampart while the resin was on her wrists. In book 1 she broke away and ran at the first burn on the rampart, and he said this to her afterward (F179, B1 ch 20).
open_errors.fix: Place the line after the rampart.

patches.find: On the rampart, with resin on her wrists and her heart running, he had said only, *Find me in daylight, when you want it.*
patches.replace: After the rampart, when she had fled him with resin on her wrists and her heart running, he had said only, *Find me in daylight, when you want it.*

open_errors.issue: Neela thinks Devan 'had never mentioned' filling her kindi. In book 1 ch 21 (F182) he told her he had filled it himself every night since the second week, spout toward the pillow because she reaches left-handed.
open_errors.fix: Acknowledge that he told her once.

patches.find: He had never mentioned it, and she had never thanked him for it.
patches.replace: He had mentioned it only once, in the dark, and she had never thanked him for it.

open_errors.issue: Janu scolds Neela for 'two nights in a wood'. Neela left Kettamala at first light on the raid day and returns about six nights later: the raid night, the days holding the House, and a day and a half on the road.
open_errors.fix: Change Janu's count to a week.

patches.find: Two nights in a wood with men, and nobody thought to hand you a plate.
patches.replace: A week in a wood with men, and nobody thought to hand you a plate.

open_errors.issue: Two day counts after the midpoint are off. Devan has avoided Neela's eyes since the ledger reading (ch 16), which is about five days before ch 23, not 'three days'. The arrow graze he has been warming cloth for happened at dawn in ch 20, about three days before ch 24, not 'four days'.

patches.find: You haven't, for three days. Not properly.
patches.replace: You haven't, for five days. Not properly.

patches.find: You've been warming the cloth for it for four days.
patches.replace: You've been warming the cloth for it for three days.

open_errors.issue: Devan tells the assize that 'last spring' a second token came off a raider's body. The narrows satchel and Bhaskaran's tally both date from this season, a few weeks before the rains. Neela was 'twenty-seven this spring' (ch 20).

patches.find: Last spring a second came off a raider's body in the lower narrows.
patches.replace: This spring a second came off a raider's body in the lower narrows.
